 :Judgment:

This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Ramamurthy (herein after referred to as the petitioner) in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 15.03.2023.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 15.03.2023 at about 7.30 a.m., when the petitioner was walking on the footpath on 1 st main road, M.C. SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6738/2023 Layout, near BGS hospital, Govindarajanagar, at that time, respondent's Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-0279 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed the Petitioner from behind,
resulting in the accident.
It is submitted that the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body due to the impact of the accident.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Blue Bliss hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.14,80,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of the notice issued to the Respondent No.1 and 2 they appeared through their Counsels and filed Objections to the claim petition.

The Respondent No.1 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
SCCH 15 4 MVC No.6738/2023 It is submitted by the respondent No.1 that the petitioner himself was tortfeasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the petitioner.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured under the respondent No.2.
It is submitted that the petitioner was not having valid driving license at time of the accident.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued private policy to the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-0279 in favour of the respondent No.1.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the accident caused by rash and negligent Ramamurthy vs Janani Tours And Resorts Pvt Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61026276/
2 driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The age,
avocation of the petitioner is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 28.02.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15.03.2023 at about 7.30 p.m., near B.G.S Hospital,
1st main, M.C. Layout, Vijayanagar, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-0279?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

3) What Order or Award?
6.

In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two SCCH 15 6 MVC No.6738/2023 witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 23 and the Respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R1 to 5.
7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order
for the following :
REASONS 8.
Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-0279 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle).

9. In this regard the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on SCCH 15 7 MVC No.6738/2023 15.03.2023 at about 7.30 a.m. when the petitioner was walking on the footpath while returning home after morning walk near 1st main road, M.C.
Layout, near BGS hospital, Govindarajanagar, the driver of the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner from backside and dashed the petitioner who was walking on the footpath,
Ramamurthy vs Janani Tours And Resorts Pvt Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61026276/
3 resulting in the grievous injuries to the petitioner.
10.

sentences.text: In order to prove the manner of the accident petitioner has produced Ex.P1 which is the copy of FIR wherein the case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for offences under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
On perusal of Ex.P2 Complaint it discloses that the case has been given on the same day of the accident and hence there is no delay in lodging the complaint.

Further documents discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle has pleaded guilty and remitted the fine amount and after investigation the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P3 for offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Hence SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6738/2023
these documents shows that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 wherein petitioner has denied that the accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

PW.1 has deposed that the road about 30 feet and there is no divider between the road and PW.1 has stated that he was walking on the left side of the road and accident has taken place at distance of 3 feet from the edge of the road.

Hence the spot of the accident also shows that the accident has taken place almost at the edge of the road and it cannot be said that the petitioner all of a sudden entered the road thereby contributing to the accident.
If the driver of the offending vehicle had controlled the speed or was cautious then certainly he could have avoided the accident.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.6738/2023 negligence on the petitioner side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross- examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of SCCH 15 10 MVC No.6738/2023 the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P5 - Wound certificate, Ex.P6 - Discharge summary, Ex.P7 - Medical bills, Ex.P8 - prescriptions, Ex.P9 - Lab reports and Ex.P10 - X-ray and on perusal of these documents it discloses that the petitioner had Ramamurthy vs Janani Tours And Resorts Pvt Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61026276/
4 sustained 1/3rd both bone or right leg fracture distal and has undergone treatment as an inpatient in Blue Bliss hospital.

sentences.text: As far as the medical bills are concerned except suggesting that these documents are got created nothing much is elicited in SCCH 15 11 MVC No.6738/2023 the cross-examination to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.

The only contention taken in the cross-examination is that much prior to the accident petitioner is suffering from heart related ailments and also has BP and diabetes and contention taken is that he has produced the bills pertaining to heart diseases, BP and diabetes.

No doubt there are certain medicines pertaining to other ailments which might have been taken in the course of treatment for accidental injuries and might be incidental to accidental injuries like diabetes and BP.
Hence in the absence of specifying the particular bills which ought to be excluding the bill of Jayadeva Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences and Research for Rs.2,230/-.

entities.text: Jayadeva Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences and Research
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Hence petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.2,89,658/-
under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P5 discloses that the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones of right leg,
fracture of right side distal radius SCCH 15 12 MVC No.6738/2023 bone, fracture of lateral malleolus on left side and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment as cause unbearable pain and petitioner cannot walk or do any work as prior to the accident.
It is also stated that the petitioner cannot stand for long time or carry or lift weight and cannot drive.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is an awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 79 years and he was working as milk vendor and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

However in his cross-examination he has deposed that he has not produced any documents to show that he was doing any SCCH 15 13 MVC No.6738/2023 cultivation and working as milk vendor and not produced any documents show to his income.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the Petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident, as per the guidelines of Lok-Adalat chart.
As per the relevant period the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 6 months.
Hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,000 X 6 = 96,000/- under this head.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:
The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit he has suffered permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
As per the evidence of PW.3 his impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that he cannot pursue his work as before the accident.

PW3 in his evidence has deposed about SCCH 15 14 MVC No.6738/2023 the physical disability sustained by the petitioner and it is admitted that the petitioner can do his work with some Ramamurthy vs Janani Tours And Resorts Pvt Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61026276/
5 difficulties.
17.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination of PW.3 he has deposed that he has treated the petitioner and the Fracture of the petitioner is united and he has issued the guidelines as per the proforma and guidelines of the gazette notification of 2018.
It is submitted that due to old age the petitioner has other ailments and he has assessed the disability only for particular limb.
It is admitted that by physiotherapy treatment the loss of range movement can be reduced.
It is suggested by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that disability assessed is on the higher side and said suggestion is denied by PW.3.

In support of the same the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has also relied on the decision in SLP No.2738-2739 of 2019, between Uttar Pradesh Road Transport corporation Vs. Vibhor Fialok and another.

entities.text: Uttar Pradesh Road Transport corporation Vs. Vibhor Fialok and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the dictum and principle of law laid down in the said decision is taken into consideration SCCH 15 15 MVC No.6738/2023 the whole body disability when compared to the particular limb disability would be 1/4th of the total disability.
The petitioner obtained treatment in the hospital as an inpatient from 15.03.2023 to 23.03.2023 and he has examined the petitioner on 21.11.2024 for assessment of disability.
PW.3 deposed that the petitioner had sustained fracture of both bones of right leg, fracture of right side distal radius bone, fracture of lateral malleolus on left side.
Hence nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.3 to disprove the disability arrived to the particular limb.
Accordingly, above mentioned disability can be read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs Union of India.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the decision supra  of the disability assessed could be taken to the whole body.
The petitioner is working as milk vending and he can continue the said even in future admittedly with some difficulties.

The evidence of PW.3 discloses that the petitioner had sustained disability of right SCCH 15 16 MVC No.6738/2023 lower limb at 17% and right upper limb at 8% and if 1/4th is taken it would be 6.25% to the whole body.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,000/- at the relevant time.

As far as,
age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P13 the birth of the petitioner is 01.01.1944.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 15.03.2023 was around 79 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '5' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.

sentences.text:
The loss of future earnings of petitioner due to his above injury and permanent physical disability comes to SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6738/2023 Rs.60,000/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 5 X 6.25%) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.
18. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

19. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:

sentences.text: The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have to taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Shriram General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Rajastan Vs.
Smt. Laxmi

Smt. Laxmi

sentences.text: reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6738/2023 in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.

20. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  96,000/-
up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses 2,89,658/-
6. Loss of Future Income  60,000/-
 Total 5,15,658/-
 SCCH 15 19 MVC No.6738/2023
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 5,15,658/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

21. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Car bearing Ramamurthy vs Janani Tours And Resorts Pvt Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61026276/
7 Reg.No.KA-01-AN-0279.

sentences.text: There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.

However the offending vehicle being insured with the Respondent No.2, it is the respondent No 2 who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, and will have to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
22. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
 SCCH 15 20 MVC No.6738/2023  ORDER  The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 5,15,658/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be SCCH 15 21 MVC No.6738/2023 deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
